pageCache.text:
Starting School in Nursery & Reception
Welcome to Vauxhall Primary School - we look forward to welcoming you and your child to our school. We have put together some useful information to help prepare your child for starting school.
Induction Process
MOUSE CLUB
We have a Summer Pack of Activities called Mouse Club Activity Cards. All of these activities you can complete at home during the summer in preparation for starting school; some of the links in the document can be reached by using your camera on your phone to access the link. Just hold up your camera and point at the scan code, where it states Scan me. This will then link you with an activity.
ALL ABOUT ME
We would also like you fill in an ALL ABOUT ME worksheet and email it back to us (along with one photo of your child, and one photo of your family) so we can make a display in your child's classroom ready for when they start. We have a guide for parents to help you complete it HERE. Please email these to us at admissions@vauxhallprimary.org.uk
Helping to prepare your child for school
We would like to recommend that you read some stories with your child about starting school. There are a few links here for you to do this. You can talk to your child about going to big school and what they will need to learn how to do. Here are some great stories, please click on each link to access the story:-
There are also some really useful games and activities to do with your child about starting school here. Please click on the link and complete the game:-
The simple things can be really helpful, too: getting familiar with numbers, letters and sounds, what their name looks like, singing nursery rhymes, and just doing things with your children like baking, getting out in the garden or your local park if you have one and simply chatting with them.
There's also advice on how to make your home a fun learning zone, and films to help your child develop independence skills like using the toilet and getting into good sleep habits.
If you've had a look at the Mouse Club Activities then you might recognise who it is giving you and your child a tour of their classroom below!
Jellybean goes to school
The Pigeon has to go to school
Topsy and Tim Start school
Harry and the dinosaurs go to school
My First Day At School
Sing some nursery rhymes together,
Documents needed by the school
At induction meetings there are also a few forms needed by the school that we would normally ask you to complete on site. You can post these to the school or email to admissions@vauxhallprimary.org.uk
Home School Agreement
Emergency Contact Collection Form
Parent Declaration Form
Additional Information
SCHOOL MEALS
Your child can either bring in a packed lunch from home or they can have a school lunch. School meals cost £2.50 a day and are paid for online via ParentPay (you will get your login details once your child has started). You can see more information from our caterers HERE and the menu for next term HERE.
Children in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2 will automatically get a free school meal as part of the Universal Free School Meals government offer (please note Nursery is not included in this offer).
However, this is not the same as Free School Meals which are provided for parents in receipt of certain benefits. If you would to check your eligibility for Free School Meals then please complete and return the form HERE - this would mean that you are eligible for discount on certain school trips and on our after school activities as well as school meals.
School UNiform
You can find information on what our school uniform is HERE and can a link to our M&S Uniform page HERE. All our new Reception children will be given a free PE Kit.
NURSERY - 30 HOURS FREe childcare
If you have a 3 or 4 year old who is due to start Nursery and you are working, you may be eligible for 30 hours free childcare.
To register, check your eligibility or find out more go to
https://childcare-support.tax.service.gov.uk/par/app/applynow
If you register AFTER 31 August, you will have to wait until January 2021 before you can claim the 30 hours free childcare. If you already have a code you will need to RECONFIRM before 31 August to keep your full-time place.
For help and more information please visit : https://www.lambeth.gov.uk/freeearlylearning or
Email: earlyyearspupilpremium@lambeth.gov.uk

In Year 3 to 6, all children follow the Reading Masters scheme, a programme devised by staff at Vauxhall Primary School.
Reading Masters is a five-day per week programme for reading fluency and comprehension. Each day a specific reading skill is taught, modelled and practised in a whole class setting.

A study by the University of York has found that Reading Masters had a positive impact on pupil progress in reading comprehension . Autism support
Autistic children benefit from structure and routine. You can help them by using visual timetables to help them see what is happening at each step of the day, so they know in advance what they will be doing next. This will relieve some of their anxiety.
You might want to set a specific place for them to do any work or tasks. At school they may have this in the form of a workstation to support their learning (see example in resources section). Each child’s workstation may differ slightly, so you could ask your child to help you set one up that will suit them or that they are already used to.

DYSLEXIA SUPPORT
Dyslexia is a specific learning difference that causes difficulty with literacy related skills. It is important to encourage children to recognise and pursue the areas in which they excel (do more of what they enjoy) and support them with the areas they find difficult.
DYSCALCULIA SUPPORT
Dyscalculia is a difficulty in understanding numbers.
https://blog.brainbalancecenters.com/2016/02/5-strategies-for-managing-dyscalculia

Black History Month 2023
Vauxhall Primary School celebrated Black History Month, with a focus on 'She-roes' - 'Celebrating our Sisters, Saluting our Sisters, and Honouring Matriarchs of Movements'. It was aimed at honouring all the remarkable Black women who have made and are still making a difference in our society.
We launched the month with an assembly that provided a taster into some of the topics and people we would be learning about . These included Faith Ringgold, Malala Yousafazi and Olive Morris. The work the children produced throughout the term was outstanding! A few children from each class showcased their work in a whole school assembly and it was clear that, as a school, we engaged with this unit of work brilliantly. Here are some of the pieces that were presented:
Year 1 presented their mind maps of women who inspire them.
Year 2 were inspired by Faith Ringgold’s artistic style to create mosaics that represent their own cultures using bright colours and showing an abundance of creativity!
Year 3 wrote a powerful class poem that explored the meaning of justice and injustice - this was inspired by the injustice experienced by Olive Morris in Brixton.
Justice is good and bad, it doesn’t matter how you got it,
Justice will always find you,
Justice is when you are treated fairly, whether it is good or not,
Justice is what is right for the world,
Injustice is racism and treating people unfairly,
Justice is good or bad and what is right,
Justice can affect us all,
Justice is a necessary in a society,
Justice is respecting everyone’s rights,
Justice is people have got what they deserve, either good or bad,
Justice is fighting for others,
Justice is joyful, thoughtful and nice,
Justice is fair. We need it.
Year 4 presented their wonderful fabric mosaic that was inspired by Faith Ringgold’s artistic style of telling stories with her art to express how their own cultures have affected the stories of their lives so far.
Year 5 showcased a thoroughly researched poster about Mae Jamison who never gave up and went on to become the first black female to go into outer space - we are capable of breaking down any barriers!
Year 6 showcased a holistic overview of the topic, creating a wonderful acrostic poem describing what it means to be a 'Sheroe'. Their posters with slogans that inspired them to be proud of where they come from was the perfect way to end our assembly.
At Vauxhall primary School we focus on celebrating the accomplishments and culture of Black people all year round with several events held throughout the year, including our 'Black History Breakfast Club'. During this event we enjoyed fruits from all the Caribbean and countries in Africa (mangoes, avocado, papaya, watermelon and dates). We learnt about the history of the fruits, how they first arrived in Britain, the reception they got and finally ranked them. Pupils discussed the many everyday fruits that are imported into Britain and have become part of our everyday life.

This year’s Black History Month celebrations focussed on the theme Reclaiming Narratives. Throughout this month, the children at Vauxhall Primary School took part in exciting workshops, assemblies and extra-curricular events which were engaging as well as informative.
During our first assembly we defined the term Reclaiming Narratives and why it is important to remember the authentic stories told by African-Caribbean people as well as understanding how the message of these stories can be diluted or lost over time. This was followed up by a series of assemblies highlighting black poets from across the world and compared their accurate depiction of their home compared to inauthentic poems, again showing how the true meaning of stories are important.
#BHM24
We were then lucky enough to have rapper and motivational speaker Alim Kamara deliver two workshops to KS1 and KS2. Alim has travelled all around the world delivering motivational talks to Prime Ministers, royalty as well as performing in national stadiums! His workshop explained how there are many misconceptions around Africa that need to be corrected, such as how big it truly is! He then explained how authentic African stories are told and told us some with his drum! He finished by empowering our children in a truly motivational way! We held a quiz in our final assembly and the children showed they absorbed the message behind our assemblies and workshop by getting some fantastic scores!
Another way to showcase authentic Black stories is through music. Music tells stories in a pure, personal form and we wanted to expose the children to that by holding a school disco. The theme was Reclaiming Rhythms: Music Beyond Borders. The children went on a journey through the decades and listened to artists from Caribbean, Africa and Britain. This took place during morning assemblies and children were given the opportunity to analyse the songs, discuss the message behind the songs and compare how music from regions has changed and developed over time. Favourites included: Soul II Soul; Kanda Bongo Man; K’naan; Ms Dynamite and Koffee! This culminated with our school disco! It was a wonderful evening where we all listened to these artists together, danced and played games!
Disco
Black History is not just a monthly celebration at VPS, we want to make it a 365 celebration. So we are committing to holding an event celebrating Black History every month until the end of the year to show our commitment to such an important cause!

Pupil Leadership
At Vauxhall Primary School, we believe that every child’s voice is vital in shaping a positive, inclusive, and empowered school environment. Our Pupil Leadership programme champions this belief, providing opportunities for pupils to lead and collaborate on key issues affecting our school community. Our Wellbeing Ambassadors, Rights Respecting Ambassadors, and Anti-Bullying Ambassadors work closely with each other and senior leaders to ensure that pupil voice is at the heart of all decision-making.
Through their roles, our ambassadors advocate for mental health, promote respect for everyone’s rights, and lead initiatives to prevent bullying. Together, they create a safe, supportive, and respectful space for every child, making Vauxhall a place where children are not just heard but empowered to make meaningful change.
